identity.title: Practical Pharmacology of the Central Nervous System
identity.subtitle: A Laboratory and Section Guide

authors.name: Dr. Riffat Ibrahim Riffat
authors.credit_line: Dr. Riffat Ibrahim Riffat, Teaching Assistant, Department of Pharmacology & Toxicology

identity.credit_policy: Four co-authors. The three associate professors are listed first because they hold the higher academic rank (user, 2026-09-28); the section slides are by Dr. Riffat Ibrahim Riffat.
identity.rework_authorised_note: Dr. Riffat Ibrahim Riffat, author of the source slides, approved rewording and improvements in chat on 2026-09-28.

domain.primary: Pharmacology of the central nervous system

figures.notes: Mechanism diagrams and drug-comparison tables; no chemical structures (user). Slide images are not carried over; diagrams are redrawn.

audience.prior_knowledge: Pharmacology 1 (general principles and autonomic pharmacology) and physiology are complete; each chapter opens with a very short recap of the essentials only.
audience.display_line: For Level 3 students of the Clinical Pharmacy Program, Pharmacology 2

goal.notes: Turn nine section slide decks into one practical book for Pharmacology 2 sections: clearer and simpler, gaps filled, same scientific scope.

language.terminology: English only; INN drug names; no Arabic text in the book.

size.restructuring_note: Chapter order is fixed by the Pharmacology 2 section schedule: 1. Alzheimer's disease; 2. Psychosis; 3. Parkinson's disease; 4. Depression; 5. Epilepsy; 6. Skeletal muscle relaxants; 7. Anxiolytics, sedatives and hypnotics; 8. General anaesthetics; 9. Local anaesthetics. Sections inside a chapter may be reordered. Target about 120-160 A4 pages.

mcq.format: Single best answer from four options (A-D); answers with short rationales in the answers section.

references.style_note: Numbered square-bracket citations; one reference list per chapter. Core texts: latest editions of Katzung, Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Pharmacology, and Rang & Dale; clinical guidelines from the last five years.

must_keep: Chapter order of the section schedule
must_not_change: No invented ISBN, publisher or copyright registration

output.fonts: Source Serif 4, Playfair Display, Alexandria (ltr-textbook-alexandria preset)

A.note: Title and subtitle accepted; four co-authors, the three associate professors first by rank; Faculty of Pharmacy, Port Said University; rework approved; nine chapters in the section-schedule order, SMR after epilepsy, cough and asthma excluded (CNS only).

B.note: CNS pharmacology; mechanism diagrams and comparison tables, no chemical structures.

C.note: Level 3 Clinical Pharmacy; Pharmacology 1 done; very short recap at the start of each chapter.

D.note: No perspective lenses; three recurring boxes: Clinical Pearl, Caution, Exam Tip.

E.note: Evaluate, then rewrite simpler and clearer and fill gaps, keeping the same scientific scope.

F.note: English source, English output, no translation.

G.note: About 120-160 A4 pages; section order inside a chapter may change; chapter order fixed.

H.note: 10 single-best-answer MCQs (A-D) and 2-3 clinical cases with answers per chapter.

I.note: Egypt; NARS Clinical Pharmacy (PharmD); Egyptian Drug Authority for marketed products.

J.note: Vancouver; Katzung, Lippincott, Rang & Dale latest editions; guidelines from the last five years.

K.note: First section Thursday 2026-10-01; the whole book is produced now; no ISBN or publisher.

L.note: Word and PDF, A4, html PDF engine, Alexandria preset fonts; palette taken from the faculty and university logos; both logos on the cover.

M.note: Domain pillars D1 mechanism and drug-class coverage 15, D2 clinical therapeutics 15, D3 drug safety 10.
